zotero.abstractNote: Implicit learning, where models learn to represent data through the optimization of an objective function rather than explicit architectural design, has become a cornerstone of modern machine learning. However, current implicit models are often tied to specific algorithmic structures, limiting their universality. In this paper, we introduce Universal Algorithm-Implicit Learning (UAIL), a framework that decouples the learning process from the underlying optimization algorithm. By treating the optimization process itself as a learnable component, UAIL enables models to adapt their implicit representations to a wide range of tasks and architectures. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach across several benchmarks, showing that UAIL achieves state-of-the-art performance while maintaining computational efficiency.
